items.question: What happens when you pluck a guitar string?
options: It vibrates and makes a sound
It changes color
It becomes longer
It disappears
items.correct_answer: It vibrates and makes a sound
items.explanation: When you pluck a guitar string, it vibrates back and forth quickly. These vibrations create sound waves that we can hear.

items.question: Put your hand on your throat and hum. What do you feel? Explain how your voice makes sound.

rubric.4: Describes feeling vibrations and explains that vocal cords vibrate to make sound
rubric.3: Describes vibrations with some connection to sound production
rubric.2: Mentions feeling something but vibration concept unclear
rubric.1: Response relates to humming but no vibration mentioned

items.question: Why can't you see things in a completely dark room?
options: There is no light to see the objects
The objects have disappeared
Your eyes are closed
The objects are hiding
items.correct_answer: There is no light to see the objects
items.explanation: We need light to see objects. When light shines on something, it bounces off and goes into our eyes. In the dark, there is no light to bounce off objects.

items.question: You walk into a dark closet with a flashlight. Draw and explain what happens when you turn on the flashlight. Why can you now see your toys?

rubric.4: Drawing shows light traveling from flashlight to objects and explanation includes light reflecting to eyes
rubric.3: Shows flashlight illuminating objects with partial explanation
rubric.2: Shows flashlight and objects but light path or reflection not clear
rubric.1: Drawing present but explanation of light and seeing not connected

items.question: What happens when you shine a flashlight through a clear glass of water?
options: Light goes through the water
Light bounces back to you
The water turns dark
The flashlight stops working
items.explanation: Clear materials like water and glass let light pass through them. This is why we can see through windows and water glasses.

items.question: You have three objects: a piece of cardboard, a plastic wrap, and a wooden block. If you shine a flashlight at each one, what will happen to the light? Draw and explain your predictions.

rubric.4: Correctly predicts light blocked by cardboard/wood and passing through plastic, with clear drawings and explanations
rubric.3: Mostly correct predictions with some explanation
rubric.2: Some correct predictions but explanations incomplete

items.question: Which device uses sound to send a message from far away?
options: A telephone
A mirror
A ruler
A pencil
items.explanation: A telephone changes your voice into signals that travel far away, then changes them back to sound so someone else can hear you.

items.question: Design a way to send a secret message to a friend across the room using only light (no talking or writing). Draw your design and explain how it works.

rubric.4: Creative design using light signals (flashlight morse code, colored lights, etc.) with clear explanation of how receiver understands message
rubric.3: Workable design with light signals and partial explanation
rubric.2: Uses light but signal system unclear
rubric.1: Mentions light but no clear communication system

items.question: A cactus has sharp spines instead of leaves. How do the spines help the cactus survive?
options: They protect the cactus from animals that want to eat it
They help the cactus walk around
They make the cactus smell good
They help the cactus fly
items.correct_answer: They protect the cactus from animals that want to eat it
items.explanation: Cactus spines keep animals away so they don't eat or damage the cactus. This is how the plant protects itself.

items.question: Birds have beaks of different shapes. Think about how a bird uses its beak to get food. Design a tool that works like a bird beak to pick up small seeds. Draw your tool and explain how it works.

rubric.4: Tool design mimics beak function with clear explanation of how shape helps pick up seeds
rubric.3: Workable tool design with some connection to beak function
rubric.2: Tool drawn but connection to beak or function unclear
rubric.1: Drawing present but not clearly a tool or related to task

items.question: A mother bird brings food to her baby birds in the nest. Why does the mother do this?
options: To help the babies survive until they can find food themselves
Because baby birds don't like to eat
To teach baby birds to fly
Because the mother is not hungry
items.correct_answer: To help the babies survive until they can find food themselves
items.explanation: Parent birds feed their young because baby birds cannot fly or find food on their own. This behavior helps baby birds survive.

items.question: Think about how a mother cat takes care of her kittens. Describe two things the mother cat does to help her kittens survive. Why are these behaviors important?

rubric.4: Identifies two behaviors (feeding, cleaning, protecting, teaching) with clear explanation of how each helps survival
rubric.3: Two behaviors with some survival connection
rubric.2: One behavior clearly explained or two without connection to survival
rubric.1: Mentions cat care but behaviors not specific to survival

items.question: A puppy looks a lot like its mother dog but has slightly different colored spots. What is this an example of?
options: Young animals are similar but not exactly like their parents
Puppies and adult dogs are completely different
All dogs look exactly the same
Spots appear by magic
items.correct_answer: Young animals are similar but not exactly like their parents
items.explanation: Baby animals inherit traits from their parents, so they look similar. But they also have some differences, like slightly different markings.

items.question: Draw a parent plant and its young plant (seedling). Show how they are the same and how they are different. Label your drawing.

rubric.4: Both plants drawn with labeled similarities (shape, leaf type) and differences (size, number of leaves) clearly shown
rubric.3: Both plants with some labeled similarities and differences
rubric.2: Both plants drawn but similarities/differences not clearly labeled
rubric.1: One plant drawn or relationship unclear

items.question: What pattern can we observe about the sun every day?
options: It rises in the morning and sets in the evening
It stays in the same place all day
It only appears on Mondays
It comes out only when we want it to
items.correct_answer: It rises in the morning and sets in the evening
items.explanation: The sun follows a predictable pattern. It appears to rise in the east each morning and set in the west each evening.

items.question: Look at the sky at night with an adult. Draw what you see. What patterns do you notice about stars? Are some brighter than others? Can you find any shapes?

rubric.4: Drawing shows stars with observations about patterns (brightness differences, groupings, shapes/constellations)
rubric.2: Drawing of stars but patterns not discussed

items.question: In summer, it stays light outside until very late. In winter, it gets dark early. What causes this pattern?
options: The amount of daylight changes with the seasons
Someone turns off the sun early in winter
The sun is broken in winter
There is no pattern to daylight
items.correct_answer: The amount of daylight changes with the seasons
items.explanation: The Earth is tilted, so different seasons have different amounts of daylight. Summer has more daylight hours than winter.

items.question: Keep track of what time it gets dark outside for 5 days in fall and 5 days in spring. Make a chart showing your observations. What pattern do you see?

rubric.4: Chart with accurate times and clear observation that sunset times change by season
rubric.3: Chart with times and some pattern observation
rubric.2: Some data recorded but pattern not clearly stated
rubric.1: Partial data with no pattern observation

items.question: Students want to keep their lunch cold until lunchtime. What information should they gather first?
options: How long do we need to keep it cold? What materials do we have?
What is everyone's favorite color?
How many students are in our class?
What day of the week is it?
items.correct_answer: How long do we need to keep it cold? What materials do we have?
items.explanation: To solve a design problem, we need to understand the requirements (how long) and resources (what materials). This helps us create a good solution.

items.question: Your pencil keeps rolling off your desk. Draw a design for something that would stop the pencil from rolling. Explain how its shape helps solve the problem.

rubric.4: Creative design with clear explanation of how shape (edges, grooves, flat surfaces) prevents rolling
rubric.3: Workable design with some shape explanation
rubric.2: Design present but shape-function connection unclear
rubric.1: Drawing with no connection to rolling problem

items.question: Two students made paper boats to float in water. One boat floated for 2 minutes. The other boat floated for 5 minutes. What could be different about the boats? What test could you do to find out which design is better?

rubric.4: Identifies multiple possible differences (shape, size, folds) and proposes fair test with controlled variables
rubric.3: Some differences identified with test idea
rubric.2: Mentions differences or test but not both clearly
rubric.1: Response about boats but no comparison or test
